keySentence: Milo learned that the most exciting adventures begin the moment you stop being bored.

facts.Page story text 1 (draft, teacher check: When Milo came back through the tollbooth he was excited to go on another adventure right away. But when he went to look for the tollbooth it had completely disappeared from his room overnight. He felt disappointed for a moment and then looked around his room with his newly curious eyes. He saw his bookshelf and his window and his street outside and everything looked somehow different. He realized that the adventure had not been inside the tollbooth — it had been inside his own attention. Now that he knew how to pay attention the whole world was ready to be his next adventure immediately. Milo learned that the most exciting adventures begin the moment you stop being bored.
facts.Page story text 2 (draft, teacher check: The morning after Milo returned from the Lands Beyond he woke up ready for more adventure immediately. He jumped out of bed and ran to where the tollbooth had been and found nothing but empty floor waiting. A note on the floor said that the tollbooth was needed elsewhere and had moved on to its next destination. Milo stood in the empty space for a moment feeling something between disappointment and understanding. Then he looked at the note itself and noticed the precision and beauty of the handwriting and became curious. He went to his window and noticed the particular quality of morning light on the buildings across the street. He sat at his desk with his homework and found himself genuinely wondering about every problem on the page. Milo learned that the most exciting adventures begin the moment you stop being bored.
facts.Page story text 3 (draft, teacher check: The disappearance of the tollbooth is the most carefully designed element in The Phantom Tollbooth's conclusion. By removing the magical apparatus, Juster forces Milo — and the reader — to confront what the story has actually argued. If the adventure depended on the tollbooth, its disappearance would be a genuine loss and the ending would be sad. But the story has been arguing throughout that the adventure depended on something else entirely — on Milo's quality of attention. The tollbooth was a training device, not a destination machine, and training devices are meant to become unnecessary. Milo has been trained, over the course of his journey, to pay the kind of attention that the Lands Beyond required. That training does not expire when the tollbooth disappears — it is now part of how Milo's mind habitually works. The ending is not a loss but a graduation: Milo no longer needs the tollbooth because he has become the tollbooth. Milo learned that the most exciting adventures begin the moment you stop being bored.
